explanation: A king of Judah, son of Rehoboam and grandson of Solomon; he reigned for three years.
Abijah's son and king of Judah after his death; known for reforming the kingdom and removing idol worship.
King of Israel who ruled at the same time as Asa; he attacked Judah and built a fortress at Ramah.
King of Aram-Damascus who formed an alliance with Asa against Baasha.
One of the two Israelite kingdoms, located south of Israel, ruled by kings from David's line.
The northern kingdom consisting of ten tribes, separated from Judah after Solomon's death.
A city near the border between Judah and Israel, where Baasha built a fortress to control traffic.
A person who speaks on behalf of God and delivers His message to the people.
The practice of worshipping false gods or idols instead of the true God.
An agreement between two or more parties to work together toward a common goal.
Improvement or change of something to make it better or more just.
